g.text: Longitudinal cross-section displaying sterile and fertile reproductive whorls

text.tspan: 1. Examine the floral cross-section and pointer lines.
2. Match labels from the Word Bank below to target slots 1–10.
4. Use the test controls below to verify your placements.

g.text: Located at the filament tip. Contains 4 pollen sacs producing microspores (male gametophytes).
The slender stalk that elevates the anther to maximize pollen dispersal by wind or insects.
Petals (Corolla) are pigmented leaves that attract pollinators. Sepals (Calyx) protect the flower while in bud.
The collective bracket on the left uniting both the Anther and the supportive Filament.
The sticky, glandular landing pad at the very apex that traps pollen grains and initiates hydration.
The long neck column connecting stigma to ovary through which the pollen tube germinates downward.
The swollen base enclosing the ovules (megasporangia). Post-fertilization, the ovary matures into fruit.
Pistil is the complete female organ (Slots 1+2+3). Receptacle (10) is the thickened floral stem attachment.
Verified Answer Key & Physiological Function Summary
Houses ovules; develops into fruit pericarp
Vascular stalk positioning anther for vectors
Attraction of biotic pollinators via optical guides
Protection of tender floral organs during bud stage
Thickened stem apex anchoring all 4 floral whorls
This will clear all placed labels and restore
all 10 draggable items back to the Word Bank tray.
